Samarkand R10 (open): Uzbekistan enter final round with one-point lead over India
rubriker._rss_content: Uzbekistan will enter the final round of the Chess Olympiad with a one-point lead after beating Armenia 3½–½ in round ten. India remain their closest challengers following a clear victory over Uzbekistan 2, while Germany, Ukraine and Hungary are two points back. Ukraine will face the hosts directly on Sunday, with India meeting Hungary and Germany taking on the Netherlands. The decisive round will begin four hours earlier than usual, at 8.00 CEST. | Photo: Rafal Oleksiewicz / FIDE

rubriker.title: Timur Turlov elected President of FIDE
rubriker._rss_content: Timur Turlov, President of the Kazakhstan Chess Federation, was elected President of the International Chess Federation (FIDE). The elections were held on 26 September at the FIDE General Assembly, alongside the 46th Chess Olympiad, in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Turlov won in the second round, with 110 votes. At 38, he becomes the second youngest FIDE President ever elected. | Picture: ChessBase

rubriker.title: Turlov Wins FIDE Presidency
rubriker._rss_content: Timur Turlov is the next president of FIDE. In Saturday's runoff in Samarkand, delegates gave him 110 votes to Wadim Rosenstein's 85.

rubriker.title: No First-Round Knockout: Turlov and Rosenstein Head to a Runoff
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE's presidential election didn't end on the first ballot. With 192 votes cast in Samarkand on Saturday, Timur Turlov topped the field with 96, Wadim Rosenstein took 76, and Jan Henric Buettner trailed with 20. None of the three tickets cleared the majority needed to win outright, so the congress moves to a second round between the top two finishers: Turlov and Rosenstein.
